messages.subject: Re: Parallel computing with Rserve
messages.body_plain:
Simon Urbanek <simon.urbanek <at> r-project.org> writes:

> 
> On Sep 30, 2014, at 9:33 AM, hseshadri <hemaseshadri <at> gmail.com> 
wrote:
> 
> > Will Rserve work with doParallel and snow packages? 
> 
> Yes


> 
> > I understand you can use Java's multithreading to improve the computing 
speed 
> > per machine since Rserve can fork new process for each client. I want to 
> > incorporate multiple machines to reduce the computation time. Can I 
still use 
> > Rserve? What packages will work with Rserve well.
> > 
> 
> Yes. The only issue you have to be aware of is that fork() shares all 
descriptors, so you don't want to create
> clusters in the server, you only want to do it once you forked an instance 
for the client such that multiple
> clients don't bash each other's connections.

Can you explain this a little bit or more or some links or papers. 
Where can I find more information or examples of use of doParallel with 
Rserve. 

Rserve is thread safe per connection. When I spawn off multiple threads 
through java, I see multiple Rserves's spawned off  processor, I assuming 
you are calling this as fork(). If I 1000's of computations (eval function 
in each) to do simultaneously I want to use a cluster then how do I prevent 
this 

 clients don't bash each other's connections.
> 
> Cheers,
> S
> 
>

I think you misunderstood - if you have *separate* connections, they don't have anything to do with each other for the code that you run after you established it. You didn't say how you intend to use it - if you simply connect and run some code, then your'e safe - no matter if it is using parallel or not.

Cheers,
Simon
